name: Hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid axis
purpose: Regulates thyroid hormone production and contributes to metabolic rate, thermogenesis, growth and development.
signal: TRH stimulates pituitary TSH; TSH stimulates thyroid hormone synthesis and release. T4/T3 feed back to hypothalamus and pituitary.
feedback_detail: Circulating thyroid hormones suppress TRH/TSH drive, stabilizing the axis.
evidence_note: Core physiology is established. Chemical-specific disruption requires compound- and endpoint-specific evidence.

name: Hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal axis
purpose: Coordinates reproductive development, gametogenesis and gonadal steroid production.
signal: Pulsatile GnRH controls LH and FSH; gonadal hormones act on reproductive and non-reproductive tissues.
feedback_detail: Sex steroids and inhibins usually suppress upstream drive; in the ovarian cycle, estradiol can switch to positive feedback that contributes to the LH surge.
evidence_note: Axis physiology is established; endocrine-active compounds can act at different nodes and not all compounds share the same mechanism.
source_label: NIEHS — endocrine system and EDC mechanisms

name: Hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis
purpose: Coordinates glucocorticoid responses to stress and supports energy mobilization, immune regulation and circadian physiology.
signal: CRH promotes ACTH release; ACTH stimulates adrenal cortisol secretion; cortisol acts broadly throughout the body.
feedback: Negative feedback with circadian and ultradian regulation
feedback_detail: Cortisol feeds back to hypothalamic and pituitary circuits while central clocks and stress inputs modulate axis activity.
evidence_note: Normal physiology is well characterized; exposure claims should distinguish acute stress effects from chronic endocrine disruption.

name: Growth hormone–IGF-1 axis
purpose: Coordinates growth, protein metabolism, body composition and tissue repair.
signal: GHRH and ghrelin stimulate GH; somatostatin inhibits GH. GH acts directly and promotes IGF-1 production.
feedback_detail: IGF-1 and GH participate in feedback at pituitary and hypothalamic levels; secretion is also strongly pulsatile.
evidence_note: GH secretion is influenced by age, puberty, sleep, exercise, food intake and fasting, so exposure studies require careful control of context.

name: Metabolic endocrine network
purpose: Maintains glucose and energy homeostasis across feeding, fasting and activity.
signal: Nutrient sensing drives coordinated hormonal signals that regulate glucose uptake, glycogen, lipolysis, appetite and energy expenditure.
feedback_detail: Blood glucose, nutrients, adiposity signals and autonomic inputs continuously reshape hormone secretion and tissue responses.
evidence_note: Metabolic endpoints are influenced by diet, activity, sleep and body composition; observational exposure associations require confounder control.
source_label: NIEHS — endocrine tissues and EDC research

name: Posterior pituitary neuroendocrine system
purpose: Regulates body-water balance and coordinates oxytocin signaling involved in parturition and lactation.
signal: Hypothalamic neurons synthesize vasopressin and oxytocin; axons release them from the posterior pituitary.
feedback_detail: Vasopressin is governed mainly by osmolality and volume signals; oxytocin can participate in positive-feedback reflexes during labor and milk ejection.
evidence_note: This system illustrates that endocrine control includes neural secretion and multiple feedback architectures beyond classic three-gland axes.
